maria: Running a couple nsys + perfetto captures on the 4xA100 pool for the 3B model. Observed repeated long stalls that line up with KV-cache write bursts around step ~120-140 (seq 16, batch 12). Perfetto flame shows many small write ops clustered -> possible bank thrash / uncoalesced writes. Uploading trace now.

samir: can you paste the exact nsys command you used? want to reproduce locally.

maria: sure — ran with collection of cuda, nvtx, sm__* counters: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_2024 -t cuda,nvtx -c true --sample=none --stats=true --trace-fork=true 
--duration=60 --capture-range cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=stop 
python -m redwood_infer.bench --model gpt-3b --seq 16 --batch 12 --steps 200
```
also attached perfetto link: https://perfetto.app/trace/3a1f... (private)

perf-bot: Uploaded profile artifacts: s3://redwood-profiles/2024/2024509876/trace_2024.nsight.gz. Top kernels: flash_attn_v2_forward, fused_attn_block_write, kv_cache_write_coalesce. SM efficiency for flash_attn_v2_forward: 24%. Significant stall reasons: shared_memory_write_dependency, memory_throttle.

jake: quick read: SM-eff 24% + shared mem write deps strongly points at bank conflicts. For our write pattern the KV cache writes are strided by 64 bytes per lane (non-coalesced), so wavefronts collide on the same banks every ~4 cycles. I saw similar on the 2B run a week ago.

anya: @maria do we have the per-warp memaccess histogram? perfetto has it under 'memtrace' -> 'global mem' but nsys with --trace-core-events gives better per-warp. If it's bank thrash we can try: 1) align KV write buffers to 128B, 2) introduce small software shuffle to change lane-to-bank mapping, or 3) fallback to tiled-write kernel that does per-tile coalesced writes.

maria: tried the tiled-write kernel switch via our runtime flag `--kv-write-mode=tile` on a quick canary. Results: tail p99 token latency dropped from 202ms -> 150ms on the hot window, but average token latency increased ~5% (because tiled kernel has extra reorg costs for small writes). Patch diff: 
```diff
- if (writes_per_step > 0) launch(flash_write_kernel);
+ if (writes_per_step > 64 || batch >= 8) launch(tiled_write_kernel);
```

samir: interesting tradeoff. Can we make the heuristic dynamic: look at recent write density over a sliding window and switch only if sustained? That should avoid oscillation when traffic spikes. Also add a cooldown TTL after switching.

jake: agree. Also add a quick prefetch/coalescer in the fused_attn path: coalesce writes into a staging buffer (aligned) and then do one big memcpy to KV. That removes per-lane writes and helps avoid bank flooding. Pseudocode: 
```
// in fused_attn kernel (vectorized lanes)
for each lane: staging[lane] = computed_kv; __syncthreads();
if (lane == 0) bulk_write(kv_slot, staging, sizeof(staging));
```
This buys better write parallelism at the cost of extra shared mem footprint. Need to measure.

maria: ran the bulk-write microexperiment: profile shows shared memory pressure increased but overall stalls due to memory_throttle decreased ~40%. p99 improved but p50 slightly worse (extra memcpy). Tradeoffs again.

anya: can we add auto-tuner that picks between three knobs: kernel variant (flash/fused/tiled), staging size, and cooldown TTL — and optimize for p99 under latency SLO while bounding p50 regression to <7%? We can run a small grid search on the canary cluster.

maria: plan for next steps: 1) add telemetry hooks to log writes_per_step, staging_bytes, and last_kernel_switch_ts; 2) implement sliding-window heuristic with cooldown; 3) run grid search on canary for batch in [4,8,12], seq in [8,16,32]; 4) collect nsys counters: sm__warps_active.avg.pct, sm__inst_executed, shared_load_bytes, shared_store_bytes, and mem__bytes_of_global_store; 5) triage results and roll to dedicated pool if consistent.

samir: +1. Also add a perfetto slicer annotation when runtime switches kernel so we can correlate timeline with perf artifacts.

jake: I'll prototype the coalescer and a cheap heuristics test today, ping me if you want the patch for the tiled kernel guard.

maria: thanks all — uploading the annotated perfetto and sample nsys counters to the ticket. Leaving this thread open for updates; will post results from the grid run. :rocket:
